blocks.content: Barchans are crescent-shaped dunes with tips or horns pointing downstream in the direction of the prevailing wind.

rows: At the base of mountain fronts (foothills)
At the mouth of a river (sea or lake entry point)
Poorly sorted with coarse debris near apex
Well sorted with fine silt and clay carried further
Extremely low to flat coastal plain

items: Barchan dunes have horns pointing DOWNWIND (in the direction of wind flow), a high-frequency question in UPSC and State PSC exams.
Drumlins represent GLACIAL DEPOSITION, whereas Roches Moutonnées represent GLACIAL EROSION; do not confuse the two.
Stalactites hang from the ceiling, while Stalagmites grow up from the floor; when they join, they form a limestone pillar.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Alluvial fans develop at mountain fronts where streams break onto gentle slopes, depositing coarse detritus in a fan-shaped form.
Deltas form at river mouths when river speed drops upon entering standing bodies of water like seas or lakes.
Barchans are crescent-shaped sand dunes formed by aeolian deposition with horns pointing downwind.
Drumlins are oval, streamlined hillocks formed by glacial till, giving rise to basket of eggs topography.
Stalactites grow downwards from cave ceilings while stalagmites rise upward from cave floors due to calcium carbonate deposition.
